name: application-pagination
title: Pagination
description: Navigation controls for moving between pages of a paginated list, table, or search results set.
useWhen: A dataset is too large to show all at once and is split into discrete pages.
A data table or list view needs previous/next navigation with optional page-jump controls.
Users benefit from knowing their current position within a numbered sequence of pages.
avoidWhen: The dataset is small enough to display entirely — pagination adds friction for short lists.
Infinite scroll is the preferred pattern for the content type (e.g., social feed, image gallery).
The total page count is unknown — use a simple previous/next control without page numbers.
responsiveBehavior: On narrow viewports, page number buttons collapse to show only prev/next arrows and the current page. Full numbered pagination appears at md: and wider.
accessibility: Wrap pagination in a <nav> element with aria-label="Pagination" to identify it as a landmark.
Mark the current page with aria-current="page" on the active page button.
Previous and next buttons must have descriptive aria-labels when they use icon-only treatment.

variants.title: Navigation
variants.description: Numbered page buttons with previous and next arrows — the standard pattern for paginated tables and lists.
accessibility: Wrap in <nav aria-label="Pagination">; mark active page with aria-current="page".

variants.title: Navigation (Dark)
variants.description: Numbered page navigation adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Active page and hover states must maintain WCAG AA contrast on dark backgrounds.

variants.title: Input
variants.description: Compact pagination with a text input for jumping directly to a specific page number.
accessibility: Page input requires a linked visible label; pressing Enter should navigate to the entered page.

variants.title: Input (Dark)
variants.description: Page-jump input pagination adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Input border and text meet WCAG AA contrast requirements on dark backgrounds.

variants.title: X/Y
variants.description: Minimal 'current / total' counter with previous and next arrows, for compact or mobile pagination contexts.
accessibility: Counter text 'Page X of Y' is self-describing; prev/next icons need aria-labels.

variants.title: X/Y (Dark)
variants.description: Compact current/total counter with arrows adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Counter text and arrow button colors must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark backgrounds.
